defects.message: The executed gate is not the gate declared in the card. pass_criteria.blocking_high lists D1-refutation and D7-sign, but the machine-readable defect stream emits codes D1 and D7, so unless the gate performs an undocumented mapping the high D1 and D7 defects cannot match the blocking list; D5 is omitted from blocking_high entirely. metrics_gate.json marks ipca_12m h=6 pass=true even though the card's core_rule requires no significant loss to Focus (DM p >= 0.10 or focus_ratio <= 1.05) and the recorded D5 shows focus_ratio=1.114 and DM p=0.029. The gate also lists gdp_qq h=1 and h=4 although the card says GDP is a satellite excluded from the school's gate. The card's central gate is therefore a label, not an enforced structure.

evidence.card_core_rule: Theil U <= 1.05 and MZ p >= 0.05 at h=6 and h=12; no significant loss to Focus; a documented value-added win
evidence.card_gdp_exclusion: GDP is a satellite and is excluded from the school's gate and mean rank

defects.message: No conditional prediction is tested. diagnostics.irf_signs returns np.sign of each coefficient, and diagnostics.json stores those signs under irf; every entry is +/-1.0. The card's four discriminating predictions are never simulated, decomposed, or compared with a statistical benchmark: inflation_to_policy is +1.0 even though the estimated long-run response is g1/(1-rho) about 1.917, gap_to_inflation is +1.0 despite a gap coefficient of 0.0073 (t=1.15), and the fiscal-shock prediction cannot be tested because neither the card nor the code contains a fiscal observable. The only out-of-sample comparison is unconditional RMSE/MZ/DM; a statistical AR/BVAR can match that, so the claim that a purely statistical benchmark cannot produce the conditional prediction is untested.

The NKPC's long-run neutrality is imposed by construction, not tested. new_keynesian.py computes pi_e = 1 - pi1_rel - pi2_rel, so pi1_rel + pi2_rel + pi_e is identically 1 and the critics.py D2 check abs(sum - 1) > 1e-6 can never fire. No unrestricted NKPC, Wald test of homogeneity, or standard error for the derived expectations coefficient is reported. The model's central claim that inflation is anchored to survey expectations therefore rests on an assumption; the derived coefficient 0.587 is not an estimated parameter with a t-stat, and the convergence-to-anchor prediction is mechanical.

The card's NKPC refutation condition is a negative or statistically insignificant output-gap coefficient across sub-samples. The machine-readable test uses op=abs_ge on the t-stat with threshold 1.65, so a significantly negative coefficient (e.g. t=-2.5) would pass the D1 refutation; it also uses only the full sample, not sub-samples. In this run the coefficient is positive but insignificant (0.0073, t=1.15), so D1 fires for insignificance; the test would not have fired for the sign failure the card declares. The D1 label is therefore not the declared condition.

evidence.card_condition: negative or statistically insignificant output-gap coefficient across sub-samples

defects.message: The school's two declared transmission channels fail their own restrictions. NKPC gap: 0.007259pp monthly inflation per 1pp gap (t=1.1547), economically nil and statistically insignificant. FX pass-through: -0.000596 (t=-0.1441), the wrong sign for the declared external channel. The NKPC is therefore an expectations/lag inflation equation with no operative demand or external channel; the New Keynesian label is carried by the imposed expectation coefficient, not by estimated transmission. The card's D1-refutation and D7-sign conditions fire.

The Taylor rule's high fit is mostly imposed structure. The constant is fixed at zero and r*=4.0 is calibrated; rho=0.9563 makes the rule nearly an AR(1) in the real rate, with residual autocorrelation p=1.3e-10. The R2=0.992 is not evidence for the policy block, and the Taylor principle is never tested: the long-run response g1/(1-rho) about 1.917 is a ratio of two estimated coefficients with no delta-method standard error or test, while the sign-only IRF reports exactly +1.0. The card's own prediction more-than-one-for-one is numerically true but operationally untested.

The satellite bridge is not the declared satellite. R2/R3 call fit_ar(growth.to_numpy(), 3), i.e. an order-3 or order-selected-up-to-3 autoregression, not the card's AR(1) on monthly IBC-Br growth; the claim that the R2/R3 path is identical to the IBC-Br benchmark is therefore not established. The bridge also uses the global ESTIMATION_START, not the card's 2005-01 start; the changelog identifies the pre-fix start as 2003, so unless ESTIMATION_START was also changed the bridge is fit on 2003-2004 data. GDP is a satellite excluded from the gate, but the code still reports it in metrics_gate.

The Taylor block's effective sample starts in 2006-01, one year after the card's declared 2005-01 estimation start: nobs_taylor=167 to 2019-11 implies 167 monthly observations, while IS and NKPC have 177. The diagnostics sample_start=2005-01 is the raw dataset start and masks the Taylor block's later start. The card's homogeneity and neutral-rate restrictions are estimated on a different sample from the rest of the system, contrary to the single declared start.

The economically-negligible gap threshold (0.02pp monthly per 1pp gap) is not in the card; it is a post-hoc magnitude cutoff. The code records the small gap as D7 medium, while the card's medium_defects puts a small output-gap magnitude under D4 limitations. The taxonomy matters because D7-sign is in blocking_high while D4 is not; the same fact is being routed through an unregistered threshold and the wrong code.

reasoning: The code reproduces the algebra of the IS, NKPC and Taylor equations and the as-of slice is clean, but the school's structure is not actually tested. The IRF block is only a vector of coefficient signs; the neutrality check is an identity; the NKPC refutation test uses abs(t) and would pass a significantly negative gap; and the gate marks ipca_12m h=6 as pass while the card's core rule is violated by the recorded Focus loss (ratio 1.114, DM p=0.029). The estimated NKPC has a negligible gap coefficient (0.0073, t=1.15) and a negative FX pass-through (-0.000596, t=-0.14), so the two channels the card calls refutation conditions both fail. The New Keynesian label is carried by imposed restrictions (unit-sum expectations, r*=4, zero Taylor constant) and a smoothing-dominated policy rule, not by estimated transmission; the model should be rejected under its own D1/D7 conditions, and the gate needs revision before it can be trusted.
